Assert that no rows match a condition

Source: R/ensure_none.R
ensure_none.Rd

The in-pipeline form of ensure_empty(). Instead of filtering for the violations and piping them in, pass the condition directly. The check is the same, but data itself is returned, so the pipeline continues with all rows:

Usage

ensure_none(data, ..., success_msg = NULL, warn_msg = NULL, abort_msg = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

...

Conditions that describe a violating row, as in dplyr::filter().

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when rows match and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the condition.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

df |>
  ensure_none(is.na(id), abort_msg = "Rows without an id") |>
  ensure_none(amount < 0) |>
  mutate(...)

Conditions follow dplyr::filter() semantics: several conditions are combined with &, and a row where a condition is NA does not count as a violation. Test for missing values explicitly with is.na() when they matter, or state the rule positively with ensure_all(), where a missing value is a violation.

Without a message, the condition itself becomes the message ("Found rows where amount < 0"), which is often clear enough during exploration. Write your own message for checks that stay in production.

See also

ensure_all() for the rule stated positively, where a missing value is a violation; ensure_empty(), tally_violations(), checkpoints.

Examples

mtcars |>
  ensure_none(cyl < 4) |>
  ensure_none(mpg > 40, warn_msg = "Implausibly efficient cars") |>
  nrow()
#> ✔ No rows where cyl < 4
#> ✔ Check passed: Implausibly efficient cars
#> [1] 32

# The rows of a failed check, all of them
violations(ensure_none(mtcars, mpg > 30))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 11
#>     mpg   cyl  disp    hp  drat    wt  qsec    vs    am  gear  carb
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  32.4     4  78.7    66  4.08  2.2   19.5     1     1     4     1
#> 2  30.4     4  75.7    52  4.93  1.62  18.5     1     1     4     2
#> 3  33.9     4  71.1    65  4.22  1.84  19.9     1     1     4     1
#> 4  30.4     4  95.1   113  3.77  1.51  16.9     1     1     5     2

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dplyr::starwars |>
  ensure_none(is.na(species), abort_msg = "Characters without a species")
} # }
